headline: Macro favors Capital (Labor Share 93.7, Profits/Wages +7.5%); Equities show 3M pullback in AI hardware (-15.04%) vs. IT/Staffing bounce (+0.13%)

bullets.title: Labor Share Compression
bullets.text: BLS Nonfarm Labor Share stands at 93.73 (-0.67% QoQ, -1.60% YoY), remaining structurally below the 2017=100 baseline.
bullets.reason: Real output growth is accruing to capital owners faster than compensation: nonfarm payrolls sit at 159.3M with average weekly hours capped at 34.4h and hourly earnings at $38.00/hr.

bullets.title: Profits Outpacing Wages
bullets.text: Corporate Profits-to-Wage-Bill ratio hit 0.404 (+7.50% QoQ, +22.00% YoY).
bullets.reason: BEA Corporate Profits expanded to $4,279.9B SAAR (+8.40% QoQ, +26.61% YoY) while the annualized private wage bill grew only +0.47% MoM (+4.30% YoY) to $10,827.8B.

bullets.title: Watchlist Spread Drivers
bullets.text: 3M Watchlist Spread is -15.17pp (Capital Enablers -15.04% vs. Labor-Heavy +0.13%).
bullets.reason: Short-term multiple compression hit AI hardware/power names (SMCI (-32.3%), VRT (-28.6%), NVDA (-26.1%)), while oversold IT outsourcers & staffing rebounded (EPAM (+63.0%), CTSH (+9.1%), INFY (+1.7%)). Over 1Y, hardware/grid winners (ANET (+53.1%), GEV (+42.6%), TSM (+41.0%)) still anchor the capex cycle.

bullets.title: AI & Power Capex Catalyst
bullets.text: "China's $3 billion-plus pipeline of Nvidia-powered AI data centres" (Reuters).
bullets.reason: Compute & silicon capex expansion shifting income toward capital owners. Also tracked: "Cerebras secures Microsoft as a customer" (Data Center Dynamics).

bullets.title: Workforce & Macro Signal
bullets.text: "Mining in Canada pays well but wage growth has sunk to near the bottom" (The Northern Miner) — with U.S. unemployment at 4.1% (2026-10-01).
bullets.reason: Wage or bargaining-power resilience supporting labor income share.
